hz5_war.topic: The 12 July 2006 raid, the 34-day war, stated aims, conduct and the US role

claims.text: 12 July 2006: Hezbollah fighters crossed the border, killed three soldiers in the ambush and captured Ehud Goldwasser and Eldad Regev; five more soldiers were killed in the failed rescue attempt (a Merkava tank was destroyed): eight dead that day.
Hezbollah's stated aim: seize soldiers to swap for four Lebanese held by Israel; Nasrallah: 'The only method ... is that of indirect negotiations and a swap.'

Israeli cabinet 12 July promised to 'respond aggressively and harshly'; communique held the 'Lebanese Government ... responsible for the action that originated on its soil'; cabinet: 'Israel is not fighting Lebanon but the terrorist element there'; Israel cited Lebanon's failure to implement UNSCR 1559.
Halutz was reported as saying that if the soldiers were not returned, 'we will turn Lebanon's clock back 20 years.'
War began 12 July and ceasefire took effect 08:00 on 14 August 2006 (34 days).
Hezbollah fired between 3,970 and 4,228 rockets, more than 100 a day; an estimated 23% hit built-up areas.
Israeli Air Force flew 11,897 combat missions; HRW: 'some 7,000 bomb and missile strikes'.

Israel destroyed the runways of Beirut's airport, imposed an air-and-naval blockade, destroyed bridges across the Litani and Zahrani; the Jiyeh power station strike caused the largest oil spill in the Mediterranean; overall damage 640 km of roads and 73 bridges; about 15,000 homes destroyed; civilian infrastructure damage close to $2.5bn (CDR).
About one million Lebanese displaced (HRW); 300,000-500,000 Israelis displaced from the north.
John Bolton confirmed that the US and UK, with support from several Arab leaders, delayed the ceasefire process.
Nasrallah said Hezbollah first aimed rockets at military sites and turned to Israeli cities in response to Israel's bombing of civilian targets.

hz5_toll.topic: Casualties, counting methods, Qana 2006, cluster munitions, HRW findings on both sides

claims.text: HRW documented at least 1,109 Lebanese killed by Israeli attacks, 'the vast majority of whom were civilians'; 4,399 injured; HRW investigated 94 attacks that killed 510 civilians and 51 combatants; at least 300 of the 510 were women or children.

HRW method: five months of field research, 561 deaths investigated in depth and 548 more from graveyards and hospital records; cemetery markings and 'martyr' posters used to identify combatants; list incomplete.
Lebanese government put the toll at 1,123; Higher Relief Council at 1,191. Hezbollah said 250 fighters killed; Israel's Foreign Ministry 'over 600'; a UN official about 500.

121 IDF soldiers killed; Hezbollah rockets and mortars killed 44 Israeli civilians (sources vary 43-46); at least 19 of the civilians killed were Arab citizens of Israel. HRW: 43 Israeli civilians and 12 soldiers killed by rocket attacks.

HRW: Israel 'often ... did not distinguish between military objectives and civilians'; treated south Lebanon 'effectively as a free-fire zone'; assumed civilians had heeded evacuation warnings; 'Responsibility for the high civilian death toll ... lies squarely with Israeli policies'; 'reckless indifference'.

HRW on Hezbollah: fired rockets from populated areas and stored weapons in civilian areas on some occasions; weapons in at least one Dahieh apartment building; 'a handful of instances but nothing to suggest a widespread practice' of shielding.

Israeli officials said civilian deaths resulted from Hezbollah hiding among civilians and that Israel attacked only military targets; HRW said this 'rings hollow' given officials' statements naming Hezbollah's political, social and welfare institutions as targets.

HRW's Peter Bouckaert said Hezbollah was 'directly targeting civilians'; HRW criticised use of unguided Katyushas; civilian targets appeared about four times as often as military ones in Hezbollah communiques.

Qana, 30 July 2006: initial reports 'at least 54'; HRW: 27 confirmed dead including 16 children (a 28th Qana resident died elsewhere); Israeli explanations varied (bombs missed a target 300 m away; house used by Hezbollah); an air commander: 'Had we known there were that many civilians inside, we certainly would not have attacked'. Israel then announced a freeze in air attacks.
Cluster munitions: about 4.6 million submunitions fired, about 90% in the final 72 hours; HRW found use 'indiscriminate and disproportionate'; UN humanitarian chief Jan Egeland called it immoral.

HRW: estimated failure rates of 30-40% left up to one million unexploded submunitions; by 20 June 2007 they had killed 24 civilians and injured 183; IDF said it 'mostly fired cluster munitions at military objectives in open areas'.
Winograd Commission said Israel's 'current manner of employing' cluster munitions 'does not conform to international law'.
